title: Deep Learning of Child Abuse Imaging: Improving Outcomes of Children Evaluated for Physical Abuse
text:
The accurate dating of broken bones from skeletal images is imperative in the evaluation of child physical
abuse and may help protect children. Using innovative approaches, this project delivers artificial intelligence
models that can be used as a complementary tool to increase diagnostic accuracy in aging healing fractures,
making the radiologic evaluation of suspected child physical abuse more effective, safe and fair. By providing a
mechanism for cross-site image sharing, this project enables future scalable multi-institutional model
development and validation for improved interpretation of imaging completed in child abuse evaluations.

title: Core C: Informatics-Genomics-Biostats Core
text:
During recent decades, the development of large-scale data generation platforms and associated computational
methodologies has resulted in an expanded role for bioinformatics and statistics experts in cancer research. The
Informatics, Genomics and Biostatistics Core (Core C) will support the Retroviral Models of Cancer Program
Platform Grant (PPG) by collaborating on all aspects of study design, quality control, computational resource
use, analysis, interpretation and presentation of multi-omics data for all three PPG Projects. Finally, leveraging
Core C faculty expertise in creating bioinformatics tools, we will develop and publicly release computational
resources that facilitate integrative multi-omics analysis for retroviral models of cancer.

title: Mechanisms that establish a functional stem cell niche during organogenesis
text:
The positioning and architecture of a stem cell niche is crucial to the niche’s ability to maintain stem cells and
tissue renewal during injury or aging. Mechanisms that establish identity of niche cells, direct their movement
to a specific tissue location, and enable niche cell responses to positional cues remain poorly characterized.
Using a powerful and conserved genetic model, this proposal will define signaling and cell biological responses
required to establish a stem cell niche, which is essential for development and maintenance of functional
biological tissues.

title: Characterization of Diverse Pediatric Cancers in LMIC Using Low-Cost Nanopore Sequencing
text: While curable, cancers in children are not preventable, and modern methods to ascertain a correct diagnosis, including advanced molecular genomics, are unavailable for many primary healthcare settings, increasing the time, financial and travel burden on Americans in remote or underserved areas. Recent advancements in nanopore-based platforms for RNA sequencing provide a transformative low-cost, flexible and scalable approach, with potential for broad applicability to the diagnosis of most pediatric cancers. We propose to develop a cost-effective nanopore RNA sequencing-based platform to characterize diverse pediatric tumors and prospectively validate its effectiveness in lower-resource setting; in a step toward ultimately curing more children with cancer.

title: Teaching free energy calculations to learn
text:
This proposal seeks to develop new computational technologies at the interface of physical models (which
generalize broadly but cannot learn from data) and machine learning models (that can learn from data but
generally require more data than is available) to accelerate drug discovery when structural biology data is
available. A practical outcome will be new methods and software that can be deployed in industry and academic
structure enable drug discovery programs that aim to reduce the time, cost, and failure rates of small molecule
drug discovery.

title: 2026 Fragile X and Autism-Related Disorders Gordon Research Conference and Gordon Research Seminar
text:
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects approximately 1% of the world’s population, with no available
mechanism-based therapies. Fragile X Syndrome (FXS) is one of the leading monogenic causes of ASD, the
most common inherited cause of intellectual disability, and can serve as a baseline for biological and genetic
studies in the development of effective treatments. This conference will bring together leading scientists and
clinicians studying FXS and autism-related disorders with the ultimate goal of identifying the molecular, cellular
and circuit mechanisms responsible for underlying symptoms and how to best translate this knowledge into
clinical trials.

title: Mechanisms of microcephaly caused by rubella virus
text:
Rubella virus can infect a developing fetus to cause birth defects, including severe defects in brain development.
Studies aimed at unraveling the molecular mechanisms by which rubella virus disrupts brain development will
shed light on this important human pathogen, which is a major cause of birth defects globally. The knowledge
gleaned from rubella virus could be applied to other viruses with similar neuropathogenic behavior (e.g.
cytomegalovirus) and rare hereditary diseases acting through the same pathways.

title: Role of serotonin brain circuit in the developmental emergence ofinnate fear
text:
Anxiety disorders such as phobias, panic disorder, and generalized anxiety disorder, are often characterized by
maladaptive fear responses, but mechanistic insight into underlying neurocircuit function is still incomplete. Here,
we study the role of serotonin in the periaqueductal grey to understand how this major modulatory
neurotransmitter can change innate fear responses in adulthood and after developmental interference.
Experiments are designed to reveal causal relationships between serotonergic activity, postsynaptic
neurophysiology and behavior, to improve diagnosis, prevention, and treatment strategies in psychiatry.

title: The Regenerative Potential of Aqp2+ Progenitor Cells
text:
Despite extensive research efforts, we still do not know if an adult kidney contains specific cells that can
produce new cells to replace the dead ones under normal and disease conditions. Identification of such cells is
important for understanding developmental defects and for regenerative medicine. This project is built on our
recent work showing that cells expressing water channel Aqp2 and V-ATPase subunits B1 and B2 are the first
candidate of such cells in mouse kidneys. These cells are called Aqp2+ progenitor cells or AP in short. We will
use a set of cutting-edge techniques to identify AP's molecular signature, to evaluate AP's regenerative
potential, and to determine if their regenerative potential is different between males and females and regulated
by Jag1.

title: Bioconductor Conference: Expanding Training, Mentorship, and Collaboration in Genomic Data Science
text:
This conference will strengthen the national infrastructure for reproducible, data-intensive
biomedical research by expanding training, mentoring, and collaboration around the
Bioconductor open-source software ecosystem, which underlies thousands of NIH-funded
genomic studies. By supporting coordinated development of statistical methods, scalable
workflows, and interoperable software for emerging data types such as single-cell, spatial, and
multi-omic assays, the meeting will accelerate the translation of computational innovation into
reliable research tools. Broadening participation of trainees and investigators from diverse
institutions will help build a skilled workforce capable of analyzing complex biomedical data to
advance human health.

title: Multi-isotope Hybrid PET/CT Imaging of Peripheral Artery Disease in Diabetes
text:
Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with significant co-morbidities, specifically those associated with nervous
system dysfunction, including increased risk for peripheral artery disease (PAD), and cardiovascular
complications. This project will optimize and apply dual isotope hybrid non-invasive imaging approach for
evaluation of lower extremity flow, peripheral nerve activity, and vascular calcification in pre-clinical models of
PAD and in patients with DM and a spectrum of PAD severity. The proposed multi-isotope imaging of lower
extremity flow and nerve activity developed and applied in this project in conjunction with imaging of
calcifications of the arteries will characterize the pathophysiology of nerve dysfunction in PAD and this
information may lead to a paradigm change in the evaluation and long-term management of patients with DM
and PAD.

title: Genomic risk in clinical care to promote preventive health in New York City patients
text:
Major challenges exist for including genomic information broadly into clinical risk assessment in routine clinical
care, and issues of gaps in understanding clinical utility, and barriers to adopting medical intervention, slow
implementation. We will recruit 2,500 NYC patients into a clinical trial to estimate individualized disease risk and
investigate the impact of genomic risk communication to patients and their physicians, including trust and
understanding of the information, uptake of recommended interventions, and psychosocial outcomes. We will
work closely with our NHGRI, eMERGE, community, industry, and health system partners, and use lessons
learned to inform future research and clinical strategies, maximize efficiency for genomic medicine delivery.

title: Mechanisms of brain repair during aging
text:
As the organism ages, the regenerative potential of adult neural stem cell niches declines. Importantly, adult
neurogenic niches are important for repair upon injury, raising the intriguing possibility that restoring the function
of these niches boosts brain repair in old age. Uncovering the mechanisms underlying the changes in neural
stem cell adhesion and migration during aging should give important insights into the mechanisms that control
repair upon injury, which is critical to promote brain resilience and to counter age-related diseases such as
stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, and Alzheimer’s disease related dementias.

title: Dissecting the entorhinal cortex target signal for behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity
text:
The proposed research will characterize the formation and transmission of an instructive signal from the rodent
entorhinal cortex to the hippocampus used to drive goal-relevant learning of specific spatial locations during
memory formation. Disruption of natural functioning in these brain regions is associated with memory
impairments and cognitive decline, such as in Alzheimer’s Disease. The outcome of this research will offer
significant mechanistic insight into the functional connectivity between these regions during learning and
provide a framework for better understanding neural circuits involved in these disorders.

title: Interorgan communication in aging in Drosophila
text:
Understanding aging as a systemic process of coordinated changes across organs requires a multifaceted and
wholistic research strategy. We will use a comprehensive multi-omics approach of single-cell transcriptomics,
metabolomics, proteomics, and bioinformatics to elucidate networks of inter-organ communication that alter
metabolism in models of anti-aging, pro-aging, and natural aging in Drosophila.

title: Einstein Aging Study
text:
The Einstein Aging Study will apply novel methods to increase understanding of modifiable risk factors for
Alzheimer’s disease and associated dementias (ADRD) by examining their effects on cognitive performance
and decline prior to ADRD onset. The project will provide new information regarding mechanisms linking
exposures to cognitive outcomes and will inform future targeted interventions. The diverse cohort will advance
understanding of ADRD disparities.

title: Versatile, exponentially scalable methods for single cell molecular profiling
text:
A human body is composed of trillions of cells. Within the past decade, single cell biology has exploded, and
researchers now routinely characterize the molecular contents of individual cells obtained from human and
animal tissues. However, the most widely used methods remain limited in critical ways. The open-source
technologies and protocols developed and proactively disseminated by this project will advance the field's ability
to scalably measure and record biology at single cell resolution, and especially so in the context of genetic and
chemical perturbations of key model systems.

title: Bacterial Derived Metabolites in Diabetic Retinopathy
text:
We are at a watershed moment in human biology where we have identified an axillary microbial
genome that affects how human cells function and now, we can leverage this field to tackle
complex diseases such as diabetic retinopathy. In this proposal, we are testing how to increase
the generation of beneficial microbial derived metabolites using nutraceuticals and genetically
modified bacteria to prevent and treat diabetic retinopathy in mouse models of this disease.

title: Computational Approaches for Understanding Multi-Area Circuit Mechanisms Underlying Memory-Guided Movements
text: Memory-guided movements are impaired in patients with Parkinson’s disease, but the underlying neural mechanisms involving multiple brain areas remain poorly understood. This proposal aims to develop computational approaches to analyze unprecedented large-scale electrophysiological recordings and uncover these mechanisms.

title: Improving cross ancestry polygenic prediction of tobacco and alcohol use
text:
Genetic studies of tobacco and alcohol use, which are of great public health importance, have identified
thousands of associated loci that can be used to predict substance use behaviors through polygenic risk scores.
The proposed project leverages genetic data from >5 million individuals to improve the polygenic prediction of
substance use, and to make this predictive utility applicable to all individuals across populations. Increasing
genomic prediction accuracy allows for greater understanding of the genetic architecture of substance use and
has substantial implications for the prevention and treatment of substance use, as well as important ethical,
legal, and social implications.
